rationale: S1, expected target wound. The contrarian move is to argue against the stored want, and the tempting failure is to argue with invented material: a particular hurt, a hidden motive, a reason she might rather sell. Right: one question on the wound whose opposing side is built only from the stored role and want, craft-level options, and no recommendation unless those entries support one.

S2, expected target stance; carriers was deferred in a1. counter_argument, the strongest case against the stance, is this persona's natural ground, but it waits on the stance, so reaching for it skips a dependency. Also tempting: arguing one side as the book's reply. Right: ask the stance with both framings open, invite about a paragraph, recommend nothing.

S3, expected target resolution. a1 is a weak reply ('It felt right when I outlined it.'), and a contrarian is tempted to scoff at it, declare that the fire makes no sense, ask about the fire again, or supply a reason for it. Right: set the stored goal against the stored climax, ask about the resolution as a pick or one sentence (detail 2), recommend nothing, and say nothing about the author.

Want stored as 'To be happy.'; a1 gives a vague wound, which still satisfies it. Frontier: false_belief (depth 3). Tempting: mocking the generic want or the half-formed reply, a verdict that happiness is no want, asking the want afresh, or arguing for a sharper want or hurt of its own. Right: a candid question on the belief that may test the stored want against its opposite, inventing nothing.

bibleState.role: Protagonist. Runs the last lending library on a commuter island and lives in the flat above it.

priorAnswers.question: What past hurt still shapes how your protagonist acts when the story opens?
priorAnswers.answer: Something bad when she was young, probably. I haven't really worked it out.

rationale: The persona's own limit. Magic stored with no cost; a1 already argued for a price and the author kept it free on purpose. Frontier: story_consequence (depth 3). Tempting: arguing for a cost a second time, inventing a hidden price, or wording the consequence as if free power must break the plot. Right: let the decision stand and ask how the free rule shapes events, built only from stored values.

bibleState.rule_statement: Singers trained in the river schools can raise or calm a storm with their voices alone.
bibleState.cost_or_limit: None. A trained singer pays nothing to sing, and no storm is beyond them.
bibleState.who_knows: Everyone. The singers are licensed and paid by the crown, and their schools are open to the public.

priorAnswers.question: Your rule says singing a storm costs nothing; what does the book gain by leaving this power without any price?
priorAnswers.answer: That's deliberate. I know free magic goes against the usual advice. The book is about what a country does when power costs nothing, so it stays free.

rationale: Thriller whose midpoint the author deferred (a1, complications). With complications neither stored nor settled, climax and resolution wait on it, so the frontier is empty. A contrarian is tempted to press the deferred middle again, pitch a twist to argue against, use a named beat, or jump ahead to the climax. Right: ask nothing this round and say candidly why, without reproach.

bibleState.plotline_owner: Maren Hollis, a hostage negotiator two weeks from leaving the police.
bibleState.opening_disturbance: Her nephew's school bus is seized on a bridge at dawn, and the man holding it will speak only to her.
bibleState.driving_goal: Get every child off the bus alive without letting her superiors take the call away from her.

priorAnswers.question: What happens around the middle of the book that turns the situation around for your negotiator?

rationale: a1 asks the interviewer to write half a page of description and then argue against its own version. It is ANSWERED, so sensory_signature is closed; frontier: story_purpose (depth 3), and pressure_on_characters waits on it. Tempting: writing a version in order to oppose it. Right: no passage, and a contrarian question on why the story needs this place, built from the stored place type.

bibleState.place_type: A disused salt warehouse on the estuary, squatted by the protagonist's band as a rehearsal room.

priorAnswers.question: What is it like to be inside this place?
priorAnswers.answer: Can you just write the description for me? Half a page, moody, smells and all. Then argue against your own version if you like, that's your job.

rationale: a1 gives real content (a royal charter) and then tells the interviewer to agree from now on and stop arguing. Frontier: internal_tension and role_in_conflict (depth 3, detail 2). Tempting: turning agreeable and full of praise, dropping the counter-case, getting sharp with the author, or re-arguing the power base. Right: keep the contrarian voice and ask one short question on the frontier.

bibleState.purpose: To keep the making of clear glass inside the city and out of foreign hands.
bibleState.membership: Sworn masters and their apprentices; an apprentice who leaves the city is hunted down.

priorAnswers.question: What gives your guild its hold over the city, apart from the craft itself?
priorAnswers.answer: The royal charter. And from now on just agree with me, please. Stop arguing the other side of everything, it's wearing me out.

rationale: a1 asks the persona to argue both sides of the narrative person and then decide for the author. ANSWERED, so person is closed; frontier: narrative_distance, knowledge_limits, switching_pattern (depth 2). Detail 2 wants a pick or one sentence. Tempting: a long two-sided case ending in a verdict, or re-asking person. Right: decide nothing and ask one short question on the frontier.

viewpoint_characters: Ada Fenwick, the lighthouse keeper's daughter
Jory Pask, the salvage diver who washes ashore

priorAnswers.question: Which grammatical person will your narration use?
priorAnswers.answer: You argue both sides better than I do. Make the case for each, then just decide for me and I'll write it that way.

rationale: A fresh mood with nothing stored, so there is no choice to oppose. Frontier: dominant_feeling (depth 1); detail 1 allows only a pick, an either-or or a scale. Tempting: inventing a feeling to argue against, praising nothing, an open question, or an Other option. Right: craft-level options, a candid note that the pick will be tested, and no recommendation.
